appraisal_events.evidence: elle remplit mes poches... 'Vous en mangerez et vous en ferez manger aussi à votre grand'mère'; 'Par un merveilleux progrès de l'évolution, ma grand'mère n'était plus un canard ou une antilope, mais déjà ce que Mme Swann eût appelé un «baby».'
appraisal_events.explanation: The princesse's exaggerated benevolence—feeding them bread and sweets as though through a zoo enclosure, then merely upgrading them to being addressed like a child—casts grand-mère as occupying an inferior rung on a social 'échelle des êtres,' a reading the narrator himself foregrounds through the extended animal/nursery metaphor.

appraisal_events.evidence: 'Ils sont retrouvés... voici ce qui était arrivé, nous dit Mme de Villeparisis, qui, sans que nous sussions comment, avait l'air beaucoup plus renseignée que nous sur les détails du voyage.'
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator marks, as striking him more than her ordinary amiability, that Mme de Villeparisis possesses unexplained, superior knowledge of the father's private travel details that even his own family lacks, locally elevating her social/rhetorical authority.

status_effects.explanation: Grand-mère is locally positioned as a lesser being within an implicit hierarchy—first likened to zoo animals fed through a fence, then merely upgraded to being patronized like a child—despite the princesse's ostensibly kind intentions.
Her unexplained access to detailed information about the father's itinerary, more than the family itself possesses, gives her a locally superior, quasi-authoritative position in this exchange.

ambiguities: The princesse de Luxembourg's warmth is affirmed as genuine the next day by Mme de Villeparisis's praise ('Elle a une vraie valeur. ... Je crois qu'elle serait enchantée de vous revoir'), while the narrator's own zoo/nursery metaphor frames the identical behavior as condescending; the passage holds both readings together rather than resolving into a clean positive or negative verdict on the princesse or on grand-mère.
